jobs.occupation: Team Lead & Field Service Engineer, EMEA
jobs.description:
Introduction

We are looking for an ambitious and talented Team Lead & Field Service Engineer based in Ballerup, Denmark. The ideal candidate has a minimum of 10 years of experience in servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment.

About the Role

The Team Lead for the 1st Level Service and Support Team plays a critical role in leading and developing the regional Field Service Engineering and Technical Support function across Europe. The role combines people leadership, hands-on technical support, and customer-facing field activities, working closely with the team to ensure a high level of customer satisfaction and operational excellence.

With a strong focus on customer experience, the Team Lead works in close collaboration with the Application Science Manager for the region and Regional Account Managers to ensure seamless service delivery, proactive customer engagement, and successful resolution of technical challenges.

In this position, you should expect approximately 50% travel. Travel within Europe will typically involve up to two overnight stays per trip, while overseas travel may involve longer stays. We expect 80 to 100 overnight travel days per year.

About Us

Sophion Bioscience is a leading global life science company founded in 2000 by a group of passionate electrophysiologists with the aim of making patch clamping objective and independent of user skill.

We specialize in developing and manufacturing automated patch clamp and cell line solutions. Through our comprehensive technical, biological, and application support, we help our partners advance ion channel research and drug discovery. We take the voodoo out of patch clamping, enabling faster, more accurate, and objective results for our users.

Through the continued development of our QPatch, Qube 384 and Ethica M platforms, we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

Team Leadership

• Supervision: Oversee the daily operations of the 1st Level Service Team, ensuring efficient workflows and adherence to service standards.

• Motivation: Foster a positive team environment, encouraging collaboration and professional development among team members.

• Performance Management: Conduct regular performance evaluations, provide constructive feedback, and set goals for team members.

Technical Expertise

• On-Site Service: Actively participate in on-site installations, service visits, and breakdown support activities, demonstrating technical expertise and leadership.

• Remote Support: Actively participate in remote support sessions with customers related to installations, system maintenance, and breakdown support.

Customer Interaction

• Customer Relations: Act as the primary point of contact for key customers, addressing concerns and building strong relationships.

• Feedback Collection: Gather customer feedback during service visits to identify areas for improvement and enhance customer satisfaction.

Coordination and Communication

• Escalation Management: Act as a liaison between the 1st Level Team and 2nd Level Support, ensuring effective communication and timely escalation of unresolved issues.

• Best Practices: Identify and implement best practices to improve service delivery and operational efficiency across the team.

Who You Are

You are an experienced service professional with a passion for customer success, technical excellence, and team leadership. You thrive in a hands-on environment where no two days are the same and enjoy balancing strategic leadership responsibilities with direct customer engagement.

We imagine that you:

• Have a minimum of 10 years of experience servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment.

• Have previous experience leading, mentoring, or coordinating technical service teams.

• Possess strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills across hardware, software, and integrated instrument systems.

• Are highly customer-focused and motivated by delivering exceptional service experiences.

• Communicate effectively with customers, colleagues, and stakeholders at all levels of an organization.

• Have the ability to remain calm and solution-oriented in high-pressure situations.

• Enjoy working independently while also collaborating closely with cross-functional teams.

• Are organized, proactive, and capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

• Are willing and able to travel extensively throughout Europe and occasionally overseas (approximately 80 to 100 overnight travel days per year).

• Are fluent in English; additional European languages are considered an advantage.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the hiring manager, the General Manager & Commercial Director, EMEA & RoW.

Questions

Please submit your questions through the LinkedIn application process (or to your internal recruiting contact, if applicable).

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Can you find the stories worth telling and shape how an industrial sensor manufacturer communicates?

SulfiLogger is an international niche company that develops and sells high-tech chemical sensors to industrial customers around the world. Our sensors are used in industries including wastewater, biogas, oil & gas, and aquaculture where they help our customers monitor and optimize critical processes.

We operate in a technically complex B2B environment where the value of our solutions is best illustrated through customer stories. We know there are many great stories about how our sensors create value for our customers, but we simply don't have the capacity to tell them all. That's where you come in.

About the position

The Communication Specialist role is newly created, making you the first additional member of our marketing team, where you will report to our Marketing Manager.

You will own our communications function, and we expect you to independently drive it forward with sparring and support from our Marketing Manager. You should be comfortable working in a position, where there won't be a to-do list with 12 clearly defined tasks waiting for you when you arrive in the morning. You need to identify what needs to be done, take initiative, and drive projects from idea to execution independently and without relying on agencies.

Your main responsibility will be to tell the stories of how our products create value for our customers. At the same time, you will help shape the direction of our communications and ensure consistent messaging across everything we do - from ongoing communication on LinkedIn and in newsletters to the content customers face on our website, in PowerPoint presentations, in dialogues with our distributors, and in the printed materials they receive at trade shows.

The content will primarily be text-based, including case studies, customer success stories, blog posts, LinkedIn posts, and articles for industry publications. But we also want to make greater use of video-based content.

The ideal candidate

The ideal candidate has a background in communications, corporate communications, marketing, or a similar field, and at least two years of experience with B2B communications, either in-house or from an agency.

It is not important that you know anything about industrial sensors, biogas, or wastewater. What is important is that you:

• are curious, proactive, and persistent when it comes to finding the stories worth telling

• can understand technical and complex topics, identify the value our solutions provide, and communicate it in a relevant and engaging way

• can think strategically - but also get things done

• write fluent and professional English

Any additional skills is a plus. This could, for example, be within video, design and layout, web, AI, SEO/GEO, or similar areas.

What we offer

At SulfiLogger, you will join an international growth company where there is plenty of opportunities for executing on new ideas fast. You will have a high degree of independence and responsibility in your daily work, the opportunity to set the direction of our communications, and significant influence on shaping the role itself.

We are based near Egå Engsø in Risskov, with easy access by bus and letbane. You will be part of a team of more than 40 colleagues here, and we also have a division in Houston that you will support as part of your role. You can expect a good and inclusive working environment, free breakfast and lunch daily, and a high degree of flexibility in your daily work.

Practical information

• Working hours: 37 hours/week (or the possibility of part-time if preferred)

• Location: Risskov (limited opportunity for working from home)

• Salary: Based on qualifications

• Start date: As soon as possible

• We invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply quickly

• For more information: Contact Marketing Manager Peter Madsen at pem@sulfilogger.com

jobs.occupation: Software Manager – Life Science Instrument Software | Copenhagen/Ballerup, Denmark
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Software Manager to lead a team of software engineers building software for automated life science instruments. This role is for a leader with clarity, drive and curiosity — someone who can help people grow, make delivery more predictable, and shape how we use AI in everyday development. You may already be an experienced manager, or ready for your next leadership step; what matters most is your ability to create direction, build trust, and turn ambition into progress.

About the role

You lead a team of eight software engineers (frontend, backend and DevOps), report to the VP of R&D, and join the R&D management team. You own the software roadmap together with Product Management and hold budget responsibility for the function. The role is based in Ballerup, in the Copenhagen area.

Day to day you work closely with Product Management, System Engineering, Hardware, Bioscience, Quality and Technical Support. A lot of the work happens in the room rather than in documents: quick alignment at a desk, a shared look at test data, and a decision taken the same afternoon. That closeness is what makes our pace possible, and protecting the energy and team spirit that comes with it is part of your job.

What matters most to us

• Execution and structure. You know software development best practice and can turn priorities into a clear and structured plan the team understands and believes in.

• Leadership. You lead eight engineers with care and structure - performance conversations, motivation, team building - and you enjoy helping people grow.

• AI ambition. You want to change how a software team works with AI. Hands-on experience is welcome; genuine ambition and curiosity matter just as much.

What you'll do

You lead the software work from roadmap to release and set the tone for how the team collaborates:

• Own the software roadmap and release planning together with Product Management, balancing scientific priorities and business goals.

• Set the technical direction and the quality standards that keep our software robust and maintainable.

• Keep delivery predictable with clear scope, realistic timelines and visible progress.

• Lead the team day to day - hiring, onboarding, mentoring, feedback and career development.

• Shape how we use AI in software development, and share what works with the rest of the company.

• Manage the software budget and resources.

Your background

You do not need to match every point below, but we would like to hear from you if you bring a strong software foundation, leadership drive and the ambition to keep learning:

• Software engineering, computer science or similar background — either through education or equivalent practical experience.

• Solid software development experience - ideally with instruments, hardware-related or other complex product software.

• Experience guiding and mentoring engineers — formally or informally — and a strong ambition to grow into a broader leadership role over time.

• Curiosity about AI and modern ways of working, with the ambition to help the team improve how software is built and deployed.

• Fluent English.

About us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ On a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis. We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan and China.

What we offer

• Real ownership, short decision paths, and visible impact across the company.

• A collaborative, international R&D environment with flexibility in how and when you work.

• Room to shape both the technology and the way the team works, including our use of AI.

• Close interaction with colleagues across R&D - scientists, hardware engineers, product managers - and an informal tone where people help each other out.

• The energy of a scaleup: fast decisions, visible results, and a product portfolio that is still taking shape.

• A team that enjoys working together, celebrates releases, and takes team spirit seriously.

We are committed to an inclusive workplace and welcome applicants of all genders and backgrounds. If you are unsure whether you tick every box, please apply anyway - we would rather have the conversation.

How to apply

Apply via LinkedIn. If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the hiring manager (VP R&D).

Start date: as soon as possible. We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the process once we have found the right match.

Do you have a strong eye for design, and do you enjoy turning creative ideas into tangible experiences?

In collaboration with Actief Hartmanns, Axlab is looking for a Graphic Designer & Event Coordinator who wants to play a key role in shaping and strengthening our visual identity.

This is a newly created position where you will have the opportunity to make a real impact. You will be responsible for developing visual content across digital, print, and event channels while helping bring the Axlab brand to life through trade shows, conferences, and other customer-facing activities. Essential to this role are a proven track record and interest in design execution.

You will join a dynamic Marcom team that is responsible for building Axlab into the most recognized brand for bringing innovation and automation to pathology laboratories.

The role is primarily focused on graphic design, which will account for approximately 70% of your time. The remaining 30% will involve coordinating and supporting events in close collaboration with colleagues and external partners.

The role

The Graphic Designer & Event Coordinator is responsible for leading creative direction, executing graphic design, and ensuring the quality of all visual assets across digital, print, and event media. The role will bring Axlab’s graphic design capability fully in-house for the first time, owning the brand’s visual identity, building scalable asset libraries, and co-creating with external agencies where needed. Alongside design, this person works closely with the Events & Digital Platforms Manager on delivering standout experiences at trade shows, conferences, and hosted events. This role will also spend up to 30% of the time on event coordination, so there must be an interest in working on event execution.

Your responsibilities:

Graphic Design

• Contribute to creative strategy and visual concepts.

• Apply the CVI and ensure consistent brand evolution and strategy while adapting visuals to meet campaign objectives and country differences, where needed.

• Design creative assets for campaigns, events, and country requests across digital and print channels.

• Design based on knowledge of customer segmentation, journey mapping, and value proposition frameworks.

• Work with agencies, the CMO, and the Director, Marcom to evolve the brand and marketing materials, as needed.

• Create asset libraries to support scalability and efficiency.

• Maintain updated files across our systems.

• Use relevant AI and digital design tools to improve creativity, efficiency, and workflows.

Event Coordination

• Planning & logistics: managing the end-to-end event timeline from brief to debrief, coordinating booth/space bookings, A/V, catering, and floor logistics. For trade shows specifically: managing exhibit builds, shipping, and setup/teardown.

• Vendor & supplier management: sourcing and briefing vendors (printers, fabricators, AV, promotional items), negotiating contracts, and holding suppliers accountable for timelines and budgets.

• Budget tracking: tracking spending against actuals, reconciling invoices post-event.

• Marketing & materials coordination: create and deliver event assets on time (signage, collateral, giveaways, digital screens, presentations).

• Stakeholder coordination: Work with Events & Digital Platforms Manager on aligning internal teams (sales, product, marcom) on event goals, speaker/demo needs, and who's attending from the company.

• Post-event reporting: capturing leads, attendance metrics, and ROI data; documenting lessons learned for next time.

The primary working language for this role is English, but Danish is a plus. The candidate should expect to travel up to 30% during certain periods.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a creative and proactive designer who enjoys turning ideas into clear and engaging visual communication.

• A bachelor’s degree or higher in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or another relevant design field

• 3-5 years of graphic design experience (healthcare industry or other regulated industry, or marketing agency experience preferred)

• Design Expertise: Strong understanding of composition, color, hierarchy, and design best practices, along with a portfolio showcasing diverse projects across digital and print formats.

• Technical Proficiency: Mastery of Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. Experience with AI design tools is a plus.

• Brand Stewardship: Proven ability to apply and assist in the evolution of a Corporate Visual Identity, maintaining consistency across a wide range of asset types while allowing for project-level creative flexibility.

• Commercial & Business Mindset: Understanding of marketing goals, customer value propositions, and how visual design supports pipeline, brand awareness, and commercial objectives.

• Openness to Event Execution (required): Genuine interest in spending up to 30% of the time on event coordination, including hands-on execution, occasional travel, and learning new processes and tools on the job.

A role with both creativity and impact

This is an opportunity to make a visible impact. You will be the first dedicated graphic design resource in-house and will therefore have considerable influence over how we develop and manage our visual identity.

You will combine creative freedom with ownership and structure, working across various projects and collaborating with colleagues, suppliers, and agencies.

The role also offers the opportunity to develop your skills beyond traditional graphic design, particularly within event execution, project coordination, digital tools, and AI-supported creative workflows.

jobs.occupation: Klinikassistent til hårtransplantation / Clinical Assistant – Hair Restoration
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Private Clinic på Frederiksberg søger en engageret og ansvarsbevidst klinikassistent til vores team.

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer ugentligt og omfatter primært praktisk og klinisk assistance i forbindelse med klinikkens behandlinger inden for hårtransplantation og hair restoration.

Arbejdsopgaverne omfatter blandt andet klargøring af behandlingsrum, instrumenter og udstyr, assistance før, under og efter hårtransplantationsbehandlinger, praktisk hjælp ved håndtering og klargøring af grafts efter oplæring og instruktion, modtagelse og forberedelse af patienter, patientvejledning før og efter behandling samt lettere dokumentation og administrative opgaver.

Vi forventer, at du er ansvarsbevidst, omhyggelig og struktureret, har gode samarbejdsevner og interesse for klinisk arbejde og patientkontakt. Du skal være indstillet på at lære nye procedurer og arbejdsmetoder og kunne arbejde både selvstændigt og som en del af et team.

Erfaring fra klinik, sundhedssektoren, kosmetiske behandlinger eller hårtransplantation er en fordel, men ikke et krav. Relevant oplæring vil blive tilbudt.

Ansættelse: Fuldtid, 37 timer ugentligt
Arbejdssted: Copenhagen Private Clinic, Frederiksberg
Tiltrædelse: Efter aftale
Løn og ansættelsesvilkår: Efter kvalifikationer og nærmere aftale.

Ansøgning og CV sendes til Copenhagen Private Clinic.

Copenhagen Private Clinic in Frederiksberg is looking for a motivated and responsible Clinical Assistant to join our team.

The position is full-time, 37 hours per week, and primarily involves practical and clinical assistance in connection with the clinic’s hair transplantation and hair restoration treatments.

The main responsibilities include preparation of treatment rooms, instruments and equipment, assistance before, during and after hair transplantation procedures, practical assistance with handling and preparation of grafts following training and instruction, preparation and reception of patients, practical patient guidance before and after treatment, as well as basic documentation and administrative tasks.

We are looking for someone who is responsible, detail-oriented and well organised, with good teamwork skills and an interest in clinical work and patient care. You should be motivated to learn new procedures and working methods and be able to work both independently and as part of a team.

Previous experience from a clinic, healthcare, cosmetic treatments or hair transplantation is an advantage, but not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided.

Employment: Full-time, 37 hours per week
Workplace: Copenhagen Private Clinic, Frederiksberg, Denmark
Starting date: By agreement
Salary and employment conditions: According to qualifications and agreement.

Please send your application and CV to Copenhagen Private Clinic.

jobs.occupation: Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Assistant Professor in Defense-related Technologies for Unmanned Aerial Systems Engineering for Defense
jobs.description:
SDU Drone Center at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), University of Southern Denmark in Odense invites applications for positions in defense-related technologies for Drones (Unmanned Aerial Systems, UAS) at the levels of Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Assistant Professor. The positions are available from January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

What we offer
The successful candidate(s) will join the SDU Drone Center, located at SDU Campus and at HCA Airport, where we operate state-of-the-art indoor and outdoor drone laboratories. You will become part of an interdisciplinary and agile research environment with strong ties to the internationally recognized robotics ecosystem in Odense.

 

What We expect
We expect candidates to have documented expertise in systems engineering for unmanned aerial systems with demonstrated real-world applications. The successful candidate will conduct research in aerial robotics, focusing on the design and implementation of drones operating in dynamic and complex outdoor environments. Relevant research areas include, but are not limited to, autonomous systems, swarming, navigation in GNSS-denied environments, communication and coordination, airspace situational awareness and management, safety and security, and counter-drone technologies.

Experience in defense-related research and/or applications is considered an advantage.

 

Commensurate with the seniority of the position applied for, the candidates must have:

• 
Strong research and publication record;

• 
Experience with defense, industrial, public sector and/or emergency services collaboration (this is a requirement for Full Professor);

• 
Proven track record of attracting research funding (this is a requirement for Full Professor and Associate Professor);

• 
Experience with teaching and education development (this is a requirement for Full Professor and Associate Professor).

The successful candidate(s) are expected to play a proactive role in contributing to and expanding the Center’s research portfolio. This includes active participation in ongoing projects as well as the development, leadership, and coordination of new externally funded research initiatives. The candidate(s) are further expected to secure competitive national and international research funding, establish strategic collaborations with academic, industrial, and defense stakeholders, and strengthen the Center’s position in civil and defense-related drone technologies.

The candidate(s) will contribute to teaching and supervision within the Master of Science education in Drones and Autonomous Systems, which is part of the Robotics MSc programme at the University of Southern Denmark.

Research environment
SDU Drone Center conducts research in drone technologies and future drone applications within areas such as defense, infrastructure inspection, healthcare logistics, precision agriculture, nature conservation, and environmental monitoring. We are an interdisciplinary team of researchers with specializations within robotics, computer vision, software, embedded systems, and the design and construction of drone systems. Together we create drone solutions for a flourishing European society. Learn more about the center at https://www.sdu.dk/uasFor further information please contact Head of SDU Drone Center, Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz, ups@mmmi.sdu.dk,  phone: +45 6550 3570.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation). 

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration (mandatory for full professor and associate professor applicants).

• 
Summary and documentation of teaching experience (for assistant professor applicants).

• 
Research plan.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period, and appointment as an associate professor and full professor is permanent. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an associate professor and full professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level as well as scientific and teaching qualifications commensurate with the position as an associate professor or a full professor. A completed lecturer training programme or equivalent pedagogical/didactical competence development is a prerequisite. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state included the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor, associate professor or full professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Bliv en del af vores tømrerteam / Join Our Carpentry Team
jobs.description:
SEE ENGLISH VERSION BELOW

Viking Gulvservice er en veletableret virksomhed beliggende i Københavns området, som gennem årene har leveret professionelle malerydelser til en bred vifte af kundetyper. Udover gulvarbejde tilbyder vi også tømrer- og malerarbejde.

Vi søger netop nu 1-2 erfarne kollegaer til vores tømrerteam, som kan være med til at løse virksomhedens opgaveportefølje.

Har du erfaring som tømrer og er du passioneret omkring dit arbejde, så kan vi tilbyde dig en attraktiv arbejdsplads med højt humør!

 

Om jobbet:

Hos Viking Gulvservice kommer du til at arbejde med række forskellige tømreropgave, bl.a. opbygning af gulvkonstruktioner, montering af gipsplader, opbygning af lettere trækonstruktioner m.m.

Du vil blive tilknyttet en kollega, så I altid er to om opgaverne, ved små opgaver må man forvente at arbejde selvstændigt. Som makkerpar får I stillet en firmabil til rådighed med de nødvendige maskiner og værktøj.

Vi forventer, at du:

1.       Har minimum 1 års erfaring indenfor tømrerfaget

2.       Har kørekort B

3.       Er pligtopfyldende og letforståelig på engelsk eller dansk

4.       Afslutter en opgave ryddelig og kvalitetsbevidst

Vi tilbyder:

1.       Attraktiv løn

2.       Arbejdstid i tidsrummet 07:00-15:00

3.       Kollegaer du kan sparrer med

4.       Spændende og alsidige opgave

 

Lyder stillingen interessant, eller har du spørgsmål? Så er du meget velkommen til at kontakte os på mail gm@vikinggulvservice.dk

Vi ser frem til din ansøgning og cv.

Samtaler afholdes løbende med ansættelse hurtigst muligt.

ENGLISH:

Viking Gulvservice is a well-established company located in Ballerup. Over the years, we have provided professional painting services to a wide range of customers. In addition to flooring services, we also offer painting and carpentry services.

We are currently looking for 1–2 experienced colleagues to join our carpentry team and help us handle our growing portfolio of projects.

If you have experience as a carpenter and are passionate about your work, we can offer you an attractive workplace with a positive and friendly atmosphere.

 

About the job

At Viking Gulvservice, you will work on a variety of carpentry tasks, including building floor structures, installing plasterboard/drywall, constructing light timber structures, and other related carpentry work.

You will normally work together with a colleague, so there will usually be two of you assigned to each project. For smaller jobs, however, you should be comfortable working independently.

As a team, you will have access to a company vehicle equipped with the necessary machinery and tools.

We expect you to:

1.       Have at least 1 year of experience working as a carpenter

2.       Hold a valid Category B driving licence

3.       Be reliable, responsible and able to communicate in English or Danish

4.       Take pride in completing your work to a high standard and leaving the work area clean and tidy

We offer:

1.       Attractive salary

2.       Working hours between 07:00 and 15:00

3.       Supportive and experienced colleagues you can exchange knowledge with

4.       Exciting and varied carpentry projects

 

Does the position sound interesting, or do you have any questions?

You are very welcome to contact us by email at gm@vikinggulvservice.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV.

Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and we are looking for someone who can start as soon as possible.

The Impact You'll Make

As our Power Electronics Architect, you’ll play a key role in shaping the next generation of variable speed drive solutions within our HVAC and Water Drives business. By defining and driving the power electronics architecture of our frequency converters, you will develop more energy-efficient, reliable, and sustainable motor control solutions.

Your impact? You will define the technical direction of future drive platforms, ensuring optimal performance, cost competitiveness, reliability, and scalability. Your work will directly support our customers' efforts to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact while accelerating the transition toward electrification. You’ll collaborate closely with experts across hardware, software, systems, mechanical engineering, supply chain, and procurement while taking ownership of the power electronics architecture and design principles that help us build innovative products for a more sustainable future.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Define and own the power electronics system architecture for next-generation variable speed drive products

• Drive technical decisions and trade-offs across performance, cost, manufacturability, and reliability

• Lead concept development and evaluation of emerging technologies ex. Silicon Carbide (SiC)

• Collaborate across hardware, software, systems, and mechanical teams to ensure alignment with product and customer requirements

• Mentor engineers, promote best practices, and contribute to platform development and long-term innovation initiatives

What We're Looking For

• Master's degree in Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

• Extensive experience designing power electronic systems for frequency converters, drives, inverters, or similar applications

• Strong knowledge of converter topologies, power semiconductor technologies, and system-level architecture development

• Experience with simulation and modeling tools such as PLECS, MATLAB/Simulink, or equivalent tools

• Strong analytical, communication, and collaboration skills, combined with the ability to influence technical direction across multidisciplinary teams

About the team 👥

Product Management at Performativ is responsible for deciding what we build, why we build it, and whether it delivers the intended result. We own the roadmap, shape the solution, make the trade-offs, and follow each product through to adoption.

We work directly with engineers and spend meaningful time with clients. There is no layer of process separating Product from the people building or using the platform.

We are a small team working across a large product surface: portfolio management, reporting, trading, compliance, client engagement, and the data and integrations that connect it all. Every roadmap decision comes with an opportunity cost. Our job is to make those decisions with conviction—and take responsibility for the outcome.

About the role 🎯

We are looking for a Domain Expert & Product Owner to help shape and own our wealth management platform and its underlying data layer.

This role sits at the intersection of financial-domain expertise, product management, and technology. You will help set product direction based on client needs, market understanding, and Performativ’s wider business goals. You will turn complex financial workflows into clear, reusable product capabilities that solve real problems without compromising the coherence of the platform.

The problems you might work on range from defining how Modified Dietz returns should be calculated and improving the performance of computational algorithms to reducing latency in trading workflows and designing interfaces used by thousands of advisers every day.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering Managers, Technical Leads, and engineers to shape features before and during implementation. That means creating workflows, prototypes, product logic, and concrete examples—not simply writing requirements and handing them over.

You will also act as a key internal domain expert across wealth management, portfolio management, investment advice, trading, compliance, and related workflows. You will support commercial and customer-facing teams when specialist product knowledge is required and work directly with clients to understand how new capabilities fit into their wider technology and operating environment.

You will own both the ultra visible and also the less visible, but equally important, parts of the platform, including reconciliation logic, corporate-action processing, valuations, and data quality. A central part of the job is distinguishing genuine product gaps from client-specific preferences or processes inherited from legacy systems.

You need enough technical depth to earn the trust of engineers and client architects, enough commercial judgement to understand the consequences of your decisions, and the confidence to challenge a request—even when there is revenue attached—if it would weaken the product.

The role is based in Copenhagen. We support relocation for the right candidate.

What you'll do 📈

• 
Shape product direction based on client needs, market developments, business priorities, and engineering capability.

• 
Translate complex financial and operational workflows into clear, reusable product solutions.

• 
Help own and prioritise the roadmap for Performativ’s Wealth Management Suite.

• 
Evaluate opportunities based on client value, product quality, business impact, and technical feasibility.

• 
Work closely with Product, Engineering Managers, Technical Leads, and engineers to shape features before and during implementation.

• 
Create workflows, prototypes, product logic, and concrete examples that help teams align around the problem and the proposed solution.

• 
Write clear specifications that Engineering can build from without repeatedly having to interpret the underlying intent.

• 
Join client meetings, deals, and technical discovery sessions, then translate what you learn into sound product decisions.

• 
Act as an internal domain expert and support customer-facing teams when specialist product or financial knowledge is required.

• 
Identify gaps and inconsistencies across the platform and improve the overall coherence of the product.

• 
Decide what we commit to, what we decline, and why - and communicate those decisions clearly.

• 
Work with Engineering to balance speed, cost, performance, and long-term architectural integrity.

• 
Follow features into production, measure adoption and outcomes, and be honest about what worked and what did not.

What we're looking for 🔍

• 
Substantial experience in asset management, wealth management, private banking, or a closely related financial domain. Ideally, experience from a middle-office, portfolio-management, investment-operations, advice, or trading environment.

• 
A good understanding of financial products, their underlying mathematical concepts, and their operational consequences.

• 
Experience or desire to own a meaningful product or process area. Not merely coordinating tasks or administering a backlog.

• 
The ability to understand how portfolio data moves through a financial institution and where operational or data-quality problems arise.

• 
Comfort working directly with engineers and discussing APIs, data models, system integrations, and technical trade-offs.

• 
A track record of turning vague, conflicting, or overly client-specific requirements into coherent product capabilities that were built and shipped.

• 
Strong product judgement and the confidence to challenge customers, executives, and engineers when necessary.

• 
The ability to explain complex topics clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• 
Clear and precise writing. Much of your influence in this role will come through written decisions, examples, and specifications.

• 
Comfort making decisions with incomplete information and taking responsibility for the result.

• 
A willingness to travel across Europe for client work.

Preferred experience ➕

• 
Experience with portfolio-management systems or related order, execution, custody, or investment-management platforms.

• 
At least five years of meaningful product-management experience.

• 
Familiarity with financial-services regulation, such as MiFID II, EMIR, or Dodd-Frank.

• 
Hands-on software-engineering experience or a strong technical background.

• 
A practical and ambitious view of how AI can improve both your own work and the products we build.

• 
Experience replacing an incumbent system within a regulated institution such as a wealth manager, bank, asset manager, or custodian.

• 
Experience working in a high-growth or rapidly changing business.

What we can offer you 🌱

• 
Real ownership from day one. You will own outcomes, not simply administer a backlog. There are very few layers between you and a decision.

• 
Work that reaches production quickly. We ship continuously, and your work can be in the hands of advisers and financial institutions within days rather than quarters.

• 
Colleagues who set a high bar. Our team includes people from Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, BCG, Amazon, and other ambitious organisations.

• 
The opportunity to grow through responsibility. People at Performativ take on meaningful scope quickly. If you demonstrate that you can carry it, we will give you more.

• 
Direct access to founders, clients, and the market. You will be part of the conversations in which important product and business decisions are made.

• 
An ambitious mandate. We are backed by leading venture and institutional investors and are building to become a European standard—not simply another regional alternative.

About Performativ 🚀

Much of wealth management still runs on software built for another era: batch files, overnight reconciliation, manually assembled reports, and disconnected systems. Advisers and operations teams spend too much of their time working around their technology rather than serving clients.

Performativ is replacing that infrastructure. We provide one platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement, built around how modern wealth managers actually operate. Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond.

We have raised more than USD 23 million from international venture-capital firms and leading European institutional investors. Our ambition is straightforward: to become the system on which wealth management runs.

You can learn more about our product at performativ.com.

The bar 🔥

We are builders. We move quickly, speak plainly, and expect people to take responsibility for their work. Autonomy is the default, but it only works when paired with strong judgement, initiative, and follow-through.

Performativ offers unusual scope for someone who wants to take on real responsibility and build something that matters. In two years, you should be able to point to important parts of the product and say: “I built that.”

jobs.description:
Are you technically minded, curious about mechanics, hydraulics and electronics – and ready to learn a highly specialized trade?

We are looking for motivated Crane Mechanic Apprentices who want to combine hands-on experience with a strong technical education.

As an apprentice, you will also become part of a workplace where you learn by doing. You will work alongside experienced colleagues and gradually take on more responsibility as your skills develop.

What will you learn?

As a Crane Mechanic Apprentice, you will work with the construction, installation, troubleshooting and repair of truck-mounted cranes and truck chassis.

Modern cranes combine mechanics with advanced electrical, hydraulic and electronic systems, so two days are not quite the same.

During your apprenticeship, you will gain practical experience with:

• Chassis Construction and modification

• Truck-mounted cranes

• Hydraulic systems

• Electrical and electronic systems

• Diagnostics and fault finding

• Welding and metalworking

• CAD and technical drawings

• Control and monitoring systems

• Commissioning and calibration

• Safety inspections

You will also learn to use computers and specialist software for diagnostics, commissioning and calibration.

About the programme

The Crane Mechanic programme takes 4 years and combines school-based training with practical apprenticeship training in a company.

The programme starts with Basic Course 2, lasting 20 weeks. You then continue to the main course, where school periods at HEG alternate with practical training in your apprenticeship company.

At the end of the programme, you complete your final trade examination and become a qualified Crane Mechanic.

Who are we looking for?

You do not need to know everything from day one – that is what the apprenticeship is for.

We are looking for someone who:

• Has completed compulsory schooling (lower secondary education)

• Has a legal right to work on Denmark at the start of employment without the need for a work permit

• Can communicate in English

• Has a genuine interest in mechanics and technology

• Enjoys practical, hands-on work

• Is curious and eager to learn

• Has a logical and analytical approach to problem-solving

• Takes responsibility for their work

• Values quality and safety

• Enjoys working as part of a team

What do we offer?

We offer you the opportunity to build a career in a specialized technical field where mechanics, hydraulics, electronics and digital technology come together.

• A paid apprenticeship contract that offers:

• Paid accommodation and meals at the hostel during the school period

• A monthly salary from the first day of the education – in accordance with Danish regulations

• Full support with relocation, including:

• Housing

• CPR number (Danish personal ID)

• Healthcare access

• Taxes and practical matters

• You will learn Danish during your stay

Interested?

Send us your application and tell us why you would like to become our next Crane Mechanic Apprentice.

Questions?

Contact Andrei Maierean by mail anma@jks.dk

Why Join Solar?

You will have the chance to work with the latest SAP technologies in a dynamic and innovative environment. Solar offers you a flexible workplace and opportunities for personal and professional development. Your work location will be either Vejen, Aarhus or Brøndby.

jobs.occupation: Jettime is hiring Cabin Crew for our Copenhagen base
jobs.description:
Can you deliver outstanding service? Do you thrive in a dynamic environment with a varied work schedule?

If your answer is YES – then Jettime might be the perfect fit for you.

Jettime is now recruiting both experienced and inexperienced Cabin Crew to our Copenhagen Base.

As Cabin Crew at Jettime, your primary responsibility is to ensure a safe journey for our guests. In addition, you’ll play a key role in creating an unforgettable experience for our guests onboard. With our great attitude and cheerful atmosphere, every flight becomes a memorable journey. When working as Cabin Crew, your working hours follow a working schedule, which you will receive at least 14 days in advance. The job may cover all hours and days of the week, including nights and holiday days, which is why we must emphasise the importance of flexibility and adaptability. To clarify, it deviates in its entirety from a traditional 9-17 job and as Cabin Crew you can expect to frequently spend several consecutive nights away from your home base – either at one of our destinations, or at one of our Nordic bases. The great fellowship amongst colleagues in Jettime will provide many opportunities for social activities and for creating fun memories with colleagues.

What We’re Looking For

Personal competences to succeed as Cabin Crew at Jettime:

• Service-minded, flexible, and resilient

• A mature mindset

• Positive and passionate about the service industry

• Comfortable in a fast-paced environment

• Efficient, punctual, and adaptable

• Situationally aware and safety-conscious

• Experience as Cabin Crew is a plus*

Requirements

You’ll attend a 4-week Cabin Crew training course at Jettime HQ in Copenhagen.

About Jettime

Jettime provides aircraft (Boeing 737) and crew to fly on behalf of scheduled airlines like SAS, Finnair and Air Greenland and Nordic tour operators like TUI. Bravo Tours and Apollo.

jobs.occupation: Backend Developer, Data Collection and Infrastructure
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. The collection is the hard part, and it is most of this job. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry.

On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

What you will work on

• The collection and ingestion pipeline behind those numbers, together with the engineers who run it today.

• Add coverage for new search surfaces as they appear, and fix the ones we already cover when they change shape.

• Write and tune queries against very large time series data, across columnar and relational stores.

• Start with scoped changes to existing services, and grow into owning services yourself, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

What you bring

Must have:

• Solid programming fundamentals. You write clear code and can reason about what it costs at runtime.

• Code of yours running somewhere real. A production system at work, a service you host yourself, or a side project with actual users.

• Comfort in Linux. You can read logs, follow a request through a system, and find out why something is slow.

• Ownership. You take a problem, decide how to attack it, ask when you are stuck, and follow through.

Good to have:

• Distributed systems fundamentals. Queues, workers, backpressure, etc.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store.

• The network layer. Connection lifecycle, timeouts and retries, TLS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

• Web scraping or browser automation.

• AI agents. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Kafka.

All of it can be learned here.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You want to own a feature end to end, from idea to production. The problems we hand you will be scoped at first, and less so over time, and a month after something ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a narrow technical scope or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will get real responsibility earlier than most places give it. The senior engineers sit next to you, and asking them is part of the job.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English. A link to something you have built counts for a lot.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.
